axes.brief:
Constitutional competitive elections, elected Assembly presidential selection, parliamentary oversight and independent judicial review operate.
Focused six-question reassessment: The National Assembly chooses and can replace the president without a new public vote. Public participation in legislation differs from a binding signature-triggered law referendum; exceptional term issues are qualified by constitutional elections and court oversight.
axes.counterEvidence:
Corruption and unequal campaign resources qualify implementation; party recall is not voter recall, and a presidential referendum provision is not automatic citizen law repeal.
The owner-defined broader axis includes lawful delegation and direct public control; a lower numerical placement is not a regime classification. Six exact responses and response strengths remain inferred. Retained source access dates are not refreshed unless a source was actually revisited. Unchanged answers and other axes were not re-audited. The National Assembly chooses and can replace the president without a new public vote. Public participation in legislation differs from a binding signature-triggered law referendum; exceptional term issues are qualified by constitutional elections and court oversight.

answers.rationale: Competitive national elections select the Assembly that elects the President, with fixed constitutional terms and actual2024 electoral turnover in governing majority.

The retained sourced research records: Constitutional competitive elections, elected Assembly presidential selection, parliamentary oversight and independent judicial review operate. Focused interpretation: The National Assembly chooses and can replace the president without a new public vote. Public participation in legislation differs from a binding signature-triggered law referendum; exceptional term issues are qualified by constitutional elections and court oversight. This is delegation of policy decisions to independent specialists, not replacement of the electorate or a claim that all expertise is political sovereignty. A legislative mandate, appointment process and later review can coexist with not voting on every operational decision.  The described institutional delegation or bounded permission makes agreement more likely than disagreement. Universal carrying is not established by identity-document possession. The Bill of Rights protects independent remedies and association. SIM registration is not universal platform authentication; privacy does not eliminate all evidentiary search exceptions, and confidentiality disclosure protection is incomplete in practice.

The Bill of Rights protects independent remedies and association. Area-authorised security searches remain a qualified suspicionless exception despite constitutional reasonableness requirements. Earlier evidence limitations remain; new questions do not establish empirical calibration.
